title: Lebanon and Israel Agree Shortlist of Countries to Verify Hezbollah Disarmament
detail: August 7, 2026 — Following the split 7th round of Rome talks, Lebanon and Israel produced a shortlist of countries eligible to send troops to verify Hezbollah's disarmament; private security firms were vetoed by Lebanon, and the verification framework may run through UNIFIL or a new UN Security Council resolution. Final country selection rests with the United States. The next round of talks was set for early September 2026.

confidenceReason: On Aug 13, a Lebanese official denied to reporters that Beirut had agreed to any such shortlist, saying Beirut was still following up with Washington — see lebanon-denies-hezbollah-verification-shortlist-agreement (2026-08-13).

title: De la Espriella Inaugurated as Colombia's President, Signals End of 'Total Peace' Policy
detail: August 7-8, 2026 — Abelardo de la Espriella was sworn in as Colombia's 36th president in Cali, breaking with the traditional Bogotá inauguration in a symbolic rejection of President Petro's negotiated-peace approach. He vowed an 'iron fist' crackdown on armed groups including the ELN and FARC dissidents. The Ideas for Peace Foundation had criticized Total Peace ceasefires for lacking verifiable disarmament terms and clear geographic limits, arguing they let armed groups expand territory during the truce period — a critique the incoming administration cited in moving toward a militarized approach.
